description: Adapt backend for Railway deployment: configurable PORT, CORS for Railway domains, Dockerfile using $PORT, and railway.json config
steps: 1. Edit backend/app/core/config.py: Add a PORT field (int, default 8000) that reads from env var PORT. Add a CORS pattern for Railway: update CORS_ORIGINS default to include 'http://localhost:5173', 'http://localhost:3000', and add support for Railway domains. Add a method or property that dynamically checks if an origin matches *.up.railway.app.
2. Edit backend/app/main.py: Update CORS middleware to use allow_origin_regex that matches *.up.railway.app in addition to the explicit CORS_ORIGINS list. This way any Railway subdomain is allowed.
3. Edit backend/Dockerfile: Change the CMD to use shell form so $PORT is expanded at runtime: CMD uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT. Set ENV PORT=8000 as default.
4. Create backend/railway.json with Railway service configuration: specify build command (pip install), start command (using $PORT), and any needed Railway settings.
5. Verify: run 'cd /projects/sandbox/contable/backend && pip install -r requirements.txt && python -c "from app.main import app; print(app.title)"' to confirm the app loads without import errors.
acceptance_criteria: backend/app/main.py CORS middleware allows *.up.railway.app origins via allow_origin_regex
backend/railway.json exists with proper Railway config
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/contable/backend && pip install -r requirements.txt && python -c "from app.main import app; print(app.title)"
findings: All changes verified. Backend loads without errors, PORT config reads from env var correctly, CORS regex matches Railway domains. Note: railway.json was created without the schema field due to a tool limitation but this does not affect functionality.
